newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COLTS BEAT DOLPHINS TO GO 4-0 ON SEASON.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COLTS BEAT DOLPHINS TO GO 4-0 ON SEASON.

text.p: Jim Harbaugh directed a 97-yard drive for the game's only touchdown and the Indianapolis Colts knocked out Dan Marino and shut down the rushing attack of the Miami Dolphins for a 10-6 victory on Monday.

In a fierce battle of unbeaten AFC East Division leaders, the surprising Colts (4-0) continued their best start since 1977, when they won their first five on their way to a 10-4 finish and a division crown.
Indianapolis used Bernie Kosar at quarterback for all but its first possession.

For the first time this season, Miami was unable to establish a running game, managing just 28 yards after averaging 156 yards per game for the first three games. Rookie running back Karim Abdul-Jabbar, who had 124 yards last week, was held to 18 on nine rushes.

Marino was 5-of-8 for 67 yards but came up limping after the final play of Miami's opening drive. He was examined by trainers on the sideline and his ankle was iced and taped before he left for the locker room just before halftime. He was diagnosed with a sprained right ankle.
Kosar completed 15-of-22 passes for 122 yards, but the lack of a ground game left the immobile veteran at the mercy of the Colts' blitzing defence.
Harbaugh was 19-of-27 for 120 yards for the Colts, who have won four straight against the Dolphins. Zack Crockett ran for 81 yards on nine carries and Lamont Warren carried 14 times for 65 yards.
The Colts played without running back Marshall Faulk, who sat out his second straight game with a sprained foot.

Marino stuck around long enough to direct a scoring drive, completing five of his first six passes, including a 34-yarder to O.J. McDuffie to the Colts 7. But a running play went nowhere and Marino threw two incompletions before Joe Nedney's 24-yard field goal.

A Miami punt pinned Indianapolis on its 3, but Harbaugh directed the longest drive in the NFL this year. It lasted 16 plays and consumed nearly eight minutes before Harbaugh found Ken Dilger wide open in the back of the end zone for a one-yard touchdown pass with 8:51 left in the second quarter.
With Kosar at the controls, the Dolphins responded with a long drive of their own and settled for a 20-yard field goal by Nedney with 1:37 left in the half.
The Dolphins' Steve Emtman recovered a fumble by Crockett at the 50, but Miami made just one first down and punted.

Two possessions later, Colts rookie Marvin Harrison scooted 15 yards on a reverse to the Miami 26. On the next play, Crockett exploded up the middle for 25 yards, but the Dolphins stiffened and Cary Blanchard kicked an 18-yard field goal for a 10-6 lead 46 seconds into the final period.

Harbaugh saved Indianapolis when he battled Dolphins linebacker Chris Singleton for a simultaneous fumble recovery deep in Colts territory with just under 10 minutes to go. Harbaugh was shaken up and was replaced by Paul Justin for one play.
On the Colts' next possession, Harbaugh scrambled two yards for a first down before a punt by Chris Gardocki pinned Miami at its own three-yard line with 4:25 to go.
